localidad: Western slopes of the Cordillera Central; Quindío Plateu; Department of Quindío, Circasia; on the southern bank of the Roble river.
comentarios:
A very elusive bird; its plumage was not highly contrastant with the vegetation and it moved very rapidly from branch to branch. It sang very frequently from several perching points in the scrub vegetation, at ∼3-6 m in height. The scrub was on the border of a road in the countryside, and separate it from pastures. The area was formerly covered by bmh-MB. During my observations, it apparently was only resting and cleaning itself, alternating those activities with moderately long vocalization sessions. Some other species in the immediate surrounding environment were Tiaris olivaceus, Sporophila nigricollis, Zenaida auriculata, Columbina tapacolti and cf. Troglodytes aedon. I used a playback to provoque an answer call, but it didn't answer in response and limited only to look around to try to find the origin of the sound. 

Note: The recording was edited in Ocean Audio. I normalized it to -3 db and changed the recording format (mp3) into .WAV.
